headline: War at sea keeps oil above $100 while Canada looks to Alberta and Toronto votes
summary: Iran's attacks near the Strait of Hormuz kept oil near $105 all week. In Canada, a second straight month of job losses and the trade fight set the tone, with Alberta voting on Monday and Ontario cities on October 26. In the U.S., inflation and midterm politics dominated.

top.headline: Iran escalates in the Strait of Hormuz
top.what: Ship attacks near the strait continued, two vessels sank on October 14, and the U.S. and Iran now dispute whether it is open. Brent crude stayed between about $104 and $107 a barrel.
top.why: It is the biggest driver of fuel and shipping prices this year, including at Ontario pumps.

top.headline: U.S. inflation jumps to 3.7%
top.what: September U.S. consumer prices rose faster as gas hit records, and traders now see a real chance the Fed raises rates on October 28.
top.why: Higher U.S. rates and prices affect the Canadian dollar and the Bank of Canada's choices.

top.headline: Trump keeps up pressure on Canada
top.what: Trump said Canada will end up the 51st state, and Ford replied never, while U.S. tariffs keep weighing on Ontario industry.
top.why: Tariffs hit Ontario's auto, steel and lumber jobs and prices.

top.headline: Alberta votes Monday on staying in Canada
top.what: Advance polls drew large turnout and Carney rallied 5,000+ in Calgary; polls show about 70% favour staying.
top.why: A strong separatist showing would dominate federal politics.

top.headline: Canada lost 68,000 jobs in September
top.what: A second straight monthly drop pushed unemployment to 6.5%, and Ontario's rate is 7.0%.
top.why: It raises the odds of a Bank of Canada rate cut on October 28.

top.headline: Toronto mayor's race tightens as advance voting hits a record
top.what: A Nanos poll puts Chow at 51% and Bradford at 47%, and more than 222,000 people voted early.
top.why: Councils set property taxes, transit and housing approvals for four years.

top.headline: GOP senators break with Trump on Russian diesel
top.what: Twelve senators, six of them Republicans, asked Trump to cancel his deal easing sanctions on Russian fuel.
top.why: It touches diesel costs and Western pressure on Russia.

top.headline: Russian strikes cut power in Kyiv again
top.what: A Russian missile attack on October 14 left parts of Kyiv without power ahead of an EU summit where Zelenskyy appeared.
top.why: The grid war shapes European energy and aid decisions.
